summary: Journeys against a running Workshop, from another Loom host's session: inspect it, drive it, picture it. By message alone: no tool here runs a process, or reads or writes a file of its own.

tools.name: connections
tools.summary: Ask Workshop's guest door who is connected and find this session's own row, after waiting, if asked, until its load plan is at rest.
tools.description: Asks the link which far session it holds and under which name Workshop admitted it, then asks Workshop's guest door (zengine.guests) for its connection inventory and checks that the row for that far session is admitted under that name. With wait_plan it first asks the door where Workshop's load plan is and waits until it is at rest (complete, waiting on a row the weaver has to build, or refused): the door listens before the plan is realized, so a shape a row still to come declares is refused as unknown until then. Writes the inventory, and the plan's answer, as JSON. Changes nothing in Workshop.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the external host's link to the Workshop (its asks below name link 'workshop')

inputs.name: wait_plan
inputs.help: first wait until Workshop says its load plan is at rest, and say where it came to rest

outputs.name: connections.json
outputs.help: the guest door's inventory, as answered

outputs.name: plan.json
outputs.help: with wait_plan, the door's answer about the plan: state, at_rest, and the rows it names to this row

a link named 'workshop' in the session's boot plan, admitted by that Workshop
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in the session host (Workshop's shapes, declared there)
tools.recovery: 'unlinked' means the link has no far session (the Workshop is not running or refused this host: see loom-session status). A dispatch refusal from Workshop means its guests file does not let this host 'inspect'. With wait_plan, 'waiting' names the row the weaver has to build and 'refused' means the plan stopped; a shape still unknown once the plan is complete is unknown for this run.

tools.name: inspect-capture
tools.summary: Inspect a running Workshop, take its picture, press a key chord through an input session, and take the picture again.
tools.description: The journey, in order, each step checked against its owner's answer: the link's own session; this session's row in the guest door's inventory; an input session from zengine.input; a picture of what Workshop presents, fetched chunk by chunk and checked whole; optionally a picture ARMED for the next painted frame, so a capture waits at Workshop's window; optionally a hold at a release gate; an optional click that points at a pane, and the chord, injected together with settlement, so the answer comes back only once Workshop has dispatched everything the injection set in motion; the armed picture, if any; the picture after the chord; the session closed. Every failure after the session opened closes it first, and says both.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the external host's link to the Workshop

inputs.name: chord
inputs.help: the key chord to press, e.g. ctrl+p, down, escape, ctrl+shift+f -- pass empty (with a non-empty `click`) for a click-only batch, no chord following it: often the right choice for a click that may open a menu, since ANY key afterward -- even one this pane binds to nothing -- is itself a newer gesture that can make Workshop refuse the very menu the click opened as 'late' (workshop/weave_external.cpp); `clear`, `text` and `repeat` all need a chord and are refused with an empty one

inputs.name: text
inputs.help: text to type after the chord (plain order) or after clearing (clear order); needs a non-empty `chord`

inputs.name: arm
inputs.help: ask for the picture of the next painted frame BEFORE the batch, so a real capture is pending at Workshop's window until its repaint answers it

inputs.name: click
inputs.help: point at a pane before the chord: 'x,y' in a window's pixels, or 'x,y@console' / 'x,y@canvas' in a terminal's cells -- empty presses the chord with no click first. With `chord` also empty, the click is the whole batch

inputs.name: button
inputs.help: which button `click` presses: left, middle or right -- right is a pane's own second route to its context menu where the menu declares no key (a line open for typing keeps every letter, so the menu cannot also own one); ignored when click is empty

inputs.name: clear
inputs.help: a typed field's own order: Ctrl+A (select all -- component/text_box.hpp) to take the whole field regardless of its length or the caret's position, then Backspace to erase that selection (whether or not `text` follows -- an empty `text` types nothing, so the erase cannot be left to typing alone), then `text` if given, then the chord that commits it (Return) -- rather than this tool's plain order, the chord first and text typed into what it opened. Needs a non-empty `chord` to commit with

inputs.name: repeat
inputs.help: press and release `chord` this many times in the one injected batch -- a hand tapping the same key again (row down x6 to walk a list), never the platform's own key-repeat (which holds and never releases between taps); refused before it asks Workshop anything if the batch this makes would pass InjectInput's 64-moment ceiling. Ignored when `clear` is set (clearing's own order presses the chord once, to commit)

inputs.name: hold
inputs.help: hold before the chord until <run>/release/<hold> exists; empty: never

inputs.name: await_repaint
inputs.help: with arm: wait for Workshop to paint by itself before pressing the chord -- for a Workshop that changes on its own

inputs.name: await_seconds
inputs.help: how long await_repaint waits: this tool's own decision to stop waiting, never a verdict about Workshop

inputs.name: changed
inputs.help: require the picture after the chord to differ from the one before it

inputs.name: bug_after
inputs.help: raise an error on purpose after this step (inspect, open, inject) -- a tool bug, for seeing failure and cleanup

outputs.name: connections.json
outputs.help: the guest door's inventory, as answered

outputs.help: what Workshop presented once the input session was open

outputs.name: armed.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: with arm: the picture that waited at the window for the next painted frame

outputs.name: after.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: what it presented after everything the chord set in motion was dispatched

tools.name: act
tools.summary: Act on Workshop through short named steps -- chords, text, presses on painted words, on the parts a pane names, on controls and menu lines -- and check each by what Workshop says it holds, without pictures.
tools.description: Runs a JSON list of steps in order through one input session. Gestures: press (a chord, optionally repeated), type (one TextEntered moment; newlines included), open (the pane whose Pane Manager row is named pane:<office>/<pane>: the Pane Manager put on the desk when it is not, the row brought into its window with Down and Up, then pressed where Workshop says its name is -- once to choose it where it is not chosen, once to open it -- until the desk says the pane is selected; a name no row carries fails with the names the list said), select (walk a list's cursor -- the row painted with a leading > -- with Down and Up until it is the row a name names: the part the pane names so, as Info's property:Height, or, in a pane naming none, the row's text after a one- or two-column marker, up to a gap of two blanks where a value stands beside the name; bounded, and a name no row or several rows carry fails with the rows painted), part (press a part a pane names -- a row, a control, an element -- by its pane and its name, at the point Workshop gives it now, wherever the pane's last redraw put it; a name the pane does not draw fails with the names it does), into and click (press where Workshop paints a word holding some text, in a text pane or a canvas pane, found by PaneView version 7 and located by its PanePoint; into with no text presses the first word, a blank row at the point its word gives), at (press one cell of a pane's text lattice by its row and column, counted from 0 -- a text pane's painted cell, or the cell of the lattice a canvas pane sets its text on, a blank row's too -- reckoned from the reading's place and text measure), rest (move the pointer to a window pixel or a terminal cell that says which cells it means, with no button held), wheel (one wheel moment of dy and dx notches -- dy 1 away from the weaver, -1 toward -- at the point Workshop gives a part a pane names, or at its first word where the step names no part; a text pane hears it as its wheel, a canvas pane as a canvas wheel), control (a visible [label], in a text or canvas pane), menu (press the line of the menu on the screen named so -- a row's id, as its presenter names it, or the action Workshop's own menu shows -- or, where no line is, the one line holding some text). Observations: desk (wait until Workshop's own numbers for a pane -- its state, rank, keys, place and size in canvas pixels -- or for the desk hold what the step names), expect and absent (wait until a pane paints, or stops painting, a word holding some text), rows (keep a pane's words and the parts it names), picture (keep a capture), wait (a pause). Settings: settings (one pane's row of the live layout, read by message -- its revision, what the pane's declaration takes with each setting's tags, pins and summary, what the row keeps and the desk's sentence -- and, given key=value, that value written at the revision just read in the field the declaration says it takes, on or off for a flag, then read back; key=- clears it; a refused write ends the run in Workshop's words). A pane's words are its presentation: expect proves Workshop painted something, not that the owner painted about finished; pair it with the owner's own evidence. A name is the pane's: Workshop carries it as the pane said it. A part Workshop gives no point -- every place of it another part's, so no press reaches it on its own -- is never pressed: a step that would press one fails saying so. A step that presses a pane's word, part or cell (part, into, click, at, wheel, control) waits while its picture takes no press -- the one a managed opening shows, until its pane draws its own, whose words and parts Workshop says with no point -- reading the pane again; one still taking none when the step's seconds run out fails saying so. The first step that cannot be done ends the run naming its index and verb; nothing after it is sent.

tools.summary: Drive the Builder pane as a weaver would -- choose a recipe, build it, build what the project waits on, arm load-after-build, load what was built, promote, revert, or add it to the load plan -- and follow what the Builder itself says became of the press, to its own endings.
tools.description: Subscribes, through the link, to the Builder's own publications (zengine.builder's BuildAsked v1 and BuildStatus v4; the guest's row must list both under `observe`) BEFORE any key is pressed. Then presses into the Builder (closing its output reader or recipe list first), chooses the named recipe with c, and presses the act's key: build b, frontier f (build and realize what the project waits on), arm Shift+b (the load-after-build switch), load-built Shift+b (the button a finished build offers), promote Shift+p, revert Shift+r, load-it o plus the role and Return, or look (nothing: no key, no pane). Every press is settled, so everything it set in motion synchronously has arrived before it returns, marked with this run's correlation for the press: the ask this run made is the BuildAsked its press caused -- taken as ask number N, or refused in the Builder's words -- never the first status to arrive. Its operation is the one the Builder's statuses name beside that ask's number. Build, frontier, load-built and a load-it that loads now are one ask: its build must END (succeeded, FAILED, NO ARTIFACT, did not start, unknown recipe) and, when it asked for realization, its realization must END for that operation (realized or REFUSED) -- two answers, never merged; running, asked and offered are never an ending. A status about a later ask before this one's ending means another build was taken after it, and the run fails as SUPERSEDED rather than take that build's ending; another ask's refusal leaves a running build's outcome alone, and an unknown-recipe status said with no build running, over the picture of the build before it, is never that build's ending; once the build has ended, its realization is still read from that picture. The input session is given back right after the press: from then on the pane may be covered, closed or resized. Arm is confirmed by the pane's switch; promote and revert by the realization owner (zengine.realization, subscribed before the press; the row must list its RealizationAsked v1, ArtifactRealized v3 and ArtifactPromoted v2): the ask is the RealizationAsked the press caused -- taken as number N, or refused in the owner's words -- and only the ArtifactPromoted or ArtifactRealized naming N ends it, a promotion's in the same delivery and a revert's when its reload settles; a status that merely reads promoted:, or another ask's answer about the same artifact, never does; load-it by the pane's own sentence about the plan row, or, when the built product is loaded now, by that ask's operation, followed like a build. A pane's refusal ends the run in its own words. When a build does not succeed the Builder's own output reader is paged to its end and kept as output.txt. A wait that ends first, or an observation that ends (revoked, or lost with the link), is UNRESOLVED, naming the ask, the operation as far as they are known and the Workshop run that numbered them (its relay's lifetime). act=look op=N relay=R comes back to an operation: it takes no input session and needs no Builder pane, subscribes, asks the Builder where it stands (BuildStatusRequested, answered to this run alone; a row that observes BuildStatus v4 may ask it), joins that answer with every word that arrived with it before judging anything, and follows op N's build and realization separately to their endings, whether they ended before it asked or later; an answer about an ask the Builder has not numbered yet (op 0) decides nothing about op N until that ask's runner answers, so the look waits for the Builder's next word; it CANNOT ESTABLISH op N when the Builder has moved to a later ask or operation without op N's ending in any picture, has numbered no op N, or the relay is not R.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: act
inputs.help: build, frontier, arm, load-built, promote, revert, load-it or look

inputs.name: recipe
inputs.help: the recipe to choose first (its name in the catalog); empty keeps the chosen one

inputs.name: role
inputs.help: load-it: the role the artifact will hold (the office its source speaks as)

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.help: how long to wait for the Builder's answer; running out fails as UNRESOLVED, naming the operation, which the Builder carries on with

inputs.name: expect
inputs.help: succeeded, failed or any: which ENDED build outcome passes (any never accepts a build still running)

inputs.name: realize
inputs.help: realized, refused or any: which ENDED realization outcome passes; realized also needs the operation to have asked for one. A load-it row that is resolved counts as realized; pending does not, nor loading -- a load conversation whose end the Builder does not paint, confirmed at the loaded weave's own pane

inputs.name: op
inputs.help: look: the operation to come back to (its build and, when it asked, its realization), pressing nothing and reading no pane -- the way back to an UNRESOLVED run's operation

inputs.name: relay
inputs.help: look: the lifetime of the Workshop relay that numbered op, as an UNRESOLVED run names it; a different relay means that Workshop restarted and its number is another operation's

outputs.name: builder.json
outputs.help: the snapshot before; every word the Builder said after the subscription began, in order, each with its number, its cause and Workshop's history numbers; the ask (its number, taken or refused, the press's correlation) and the operation named beside it; the build ({op, outcome}) and the realization ({asked, op, outcome, detail}) as two entries; seconds from the subscription to the press, the ask, the operation, the build's end and the realization's; any confirmation; for promote/revert, the realization owner's words (owner_words) and the ask it took (number, artifact, the press's correlation) with the answer naming it; for look, the Builder's answer it joined (before); unresolved, superseded or cannot_establish (stage, op, ask -- null while never known -- and the Workshop relay that numbered them) when the run did not conclude; the subscription's own account

outputs.name: output.txt
outputs.help: only when a build did not succeed: every line the Builder's output reader showed

requires: a Workshop guest granting input and capture (not for look), and build, a version-2 guests-file power, for every act but arm and look
a guest row that may observe zengine.builder's BuildAsked v1 and BuildStatus v4 (look needs BuildStatus only)
for promote and revert: the row also observes zengine.realization's RealizationAsked v1, ArtifactRealized v3 and ArtifactPromoted v2
the Builder pane open where Workshop describes it (not for look)
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
for load-it, a Workshop whose guests file names it a development host: a weaver's host refuses a guest the role it types and the plan row it writes
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/builder --name build-game --input recipe=tower-defense --input act=frontier --input realize=realized --wait 320  |  after an UNRESOLVED run: loom-session run <dir> workshop/builder --name again --input act=look --input op=<N> --input relay=<lifetime> --input realize=realized
tools.recovery: Read builder.json and output.txt. An UNRESOLVED run names its operation once one is numbered, and the Workshop relay that numbered it; that operation keeps running in the Builder: run act=look op=<N> relay=<lifetime> to follow it again -- it presses nothing and needs no pane, so nothing is built twice, and a realization that completed meanwhile is read from the Builder's own answer. CANNOT ESTABLISH means the Builder no longer states op N here (it moved to a later ask, never numbered N, or Workshop restarted): op N's words are in the Builder's output reader (l, then the older build's output) while it keeps them. A look that is UNRESOLVED (its wait ran out while op N or the Builder's newest, unnumbered ask was still pending) names op N and the relay the same way: run it again. A SUPERSEDED run's own ending was never seen because another build was taken after it. An UNRESOLVED promote or revert names the realization owner's ask number; its answer carries that number, and nothing was pressed twice. Promote and revert change which image runs next and now respectively; neither touches source. A load refused for a changed shape leaves the running weave as it was. A refused subscription means the guest's row does not list those shapes under `observe` in Workshop's guests file: the weaver adds them; nothing was pressed. A refusal naming `build` means the guest's row lacks that power: the weaver grants it in a version-2 guests file.

tools.name: observe
tools.summary: Follow what one office of a running Workshop publishes, for a while, and keep every word: what an owner says, numbered, with every loss said.
tools.description: Subscribes through the link to one office's publications of the named shapes (the guest's row must list them under `observe`; Workshop's relay refuses anything else in its own words), takes what it is told until `seconds` pass, `count` observations arrived or the subscription ends, then releases it. Every item is kept in order in observed.json: each observation with its number, its decoded fields (decoded with the descriptors the relay sent, so this host need not know the shape), the producer and its incarnation, its cause (this run's own correlation, or 0: this tool presses nothing, so always 0) and the far host's history numbers; each Gap with how many were lost and why; the ending. It holds no input session, so it may run beside a run that does. `read_pause_ms` makes it a deliberately slow reader and `window` a small one, which is how the relay's bounds are seen: occurrences past the window are dropped, counted and said as a Gap, and a `latest` shape keeps only its newest (`coalesced`). The summary counts observations, gaps and what they lost -- a loss is never hidden.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: producer
inputs.help: the office whose publications to follow, e.g. zengine.builder or td.game

inputs.name: shapes
inputs.help: Name@version, comma-separated, e.g. BuildAsked@1,BuildStatus@4

inputs.name: latest
inputs.help: comma-separated names of shapes that are whole state: while the window is shut only the newest of each is kept

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.help: how long to follow; running out ends the run, not the producer

inputs.name: count
inputs.help: stop after this many observations (0: no count)

inputs.name: window
inputs.help: words the relay may say unacknowledged (0: its default, 256)

inputs.name: read_pause_ms
inputs.help: a pause after each word taken: a deliberately slow reader

outputs.name: observed.json
outputs.help: every item in order (observations, gaps, the ending) with the subscription's own account: words said, lost (the relay's and this client's), repeated, acknowledged

requires: a Workshop guest whose row may observe the named office's shapes
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/observe --name builder-words --input producer=zengine.builder --input shapes=BuildAsked@1,BuildStatus@4 --input latest=BuildStatus --input seconds=60 --wait 90
tools.recovery: A refusal in Workshop's words means the guest's row does not list that office and shape under `observe`, or no participant there declares the shape (the application is not loaded): the weaver's guests file decides the first. An ending `lost` means the link's session ended: what was said after the last word kept is unknown. Gaps are losses the relay or this client counted: a slower reader or a smaller window loses more.

tools.name: inventory-organize
tools.summary: Name stored Inventory entries and file them in a named folder through the Inventory owner's own operations, without an input session.
tools.description: Lists the collection (InventoryList v2), finds each rule's entry by its label (and schema, when given) plus `contains`: text that must occur in the entry's stored bytes, such as a command's field value -- a byte search, not a decoder. Every rule must match exactly one entry, or nothing is changed. Creates the folder under Root when no Root folder has that name, renames each entry at its listed revision and files it there, then lists again and passes only if every entry reads its new label in that folder. Nothing is executed and no authority is granted.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: plan
inputs.help: {"folder": name (empty keeps Root), "entries": [{"find": {"label": .., "schema": .., "contains": ..}, "label": new label}]}

outputs.name: organize.json
outputs.help: each entry's label, schema, folder and revision after the changes

requires: a Workshop guest granting inventory
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/inventory-organize --name file-commands --inputs {"plan": "{\"folder\": \"Tower Defense\", \"entries\": [{\"find\": {\"label\": \"TdCommand\", \"contains\": \"wave\"}, \"label\": \"Start next wave\"}]}"}
tools.recovery: A rule that matches no entry or several changes nothing; widen or narrow `contains`. After a partial failure the renames and filings already made remain; run it again with the same plan (a renamed entry is found by its new label) or undo them in Inventory.

tools.name: inventory-controls
tools.summary: Make a portable Inventory view of named commands, each bound to a target office and a key, through the Inventory pane's own configuration door; nothing is executed.
tools.description: Finds each control's entry by label inside `folder`, creates a single/row/column view holding the first (InventoryViewEdit create), moves the rest into it in order, binds each to `target` with its key, enables the items when asked, and sets the view's activation context. Reads InventoryViews back and passes only when the view holds the entries in order and every binding shows its target and key. Configuration runs nothing: a key pressed later runs its command only with the pressing actor's own permission for that office and shape.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: controls
inputs.help: a JSON list of {"label": entry label, "key": a chord such as alt+1}, in view order

inputs.name: folder
inputs.help: the Root folder the labels are in; empty means Root

inputs.name: target
inputs.help: the office every command is sent to when its key is pressed

inputs.name: kind
inputs.help: single, row or column

inputs.name: enable
inputs.help: turn each item's hotkey on

inputs.name: context
inputs.help: turn the view's activation context on (keys act only while it is)

outputs.name: controls.json
outputs.help: the view id and kind, its context, and each control's label, key, target and enabled state as read back

requires: a Workshop guest granting inventory
Inventory's data owner and pane loaded, with room for one more view (twelve at most)
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/inventory-controls --name td-row --input folder="Tower Defense" --input target=td.game --input controls=[{"label":"Start next wave","key":"alt+1"}]
tools.recovery: A view already created stays; move its entries back to main Inventory or leave it (a toolbox restore offers views again). A conflicting active key is refused by the pane and earlier mappings remain.
